title: Catalog of Second Chances (CSC) - Digital Database and Corresponding Interfaces for ReUse of Architectural Components (v0.6.4.4)
description:
The Catalog of Second Chances (CSC) is a prototypical digital component database. It catalogs digital representations of uniquely identifiable architectural components for reuse. Furthermore, it provides corresponding interfaces and tools to leverage them via a backend REST-API, a web-frontend as well as a interface for direct interaction within Rhino Grasshopper.

Changes in v0.6.4.4 (2026-11-03)

Grasshopper hardening, and the beta notice takes its version from the release. Run CSC_Update in Grasshopper after the server is deployed.

Fixed

  • Grasshopper, missing inputs: a component with a missing or empty input shows a warning and waits for data, instead of an error. Real failures (bad counts, unreadable data, server errors) stay errors (#32, #40).
  • Grasshopper, outputs without a result: an output with nothing to give is an empty Grasshopper tree, not <empty> or <null>, on every error path and when a component stops early. In a component that runs once per item, one missing, empty or failed item gives a null in its slot, so the outputs stay one to one with the input list; an input with no data at all gives empty outputs (#33, #40).
  • **Grasshopper, ReadFromD2P:** the Component output carries the D2P component itself, and a remark names its type. When the D2P component of an element cannot be resolved, a warning names the element; a plain tag of BakeComponents stays null without a warning (#36).
  • Beta notice: the beta banner and the beta login notice take the version from the release. The text in the frontend settings writes {version} where the number goes (#52).

Changed

  • Grasshopper, wording: the descriptions and messages of the components call a single building component an "element" instead of a "piece", as the web app does since 0.6.4.2.
  • Grasshopper, frames: the description of ApplyFrame says that its Frame output is the frame used, in the stored coordinates, and points to DisassembleComponent for the frame where the moved element sits. The Frame and BoundingBox descriptions of DisassembleComponent now say that they give the element where it sits.
  • **Grasshopper, ReinforcementLayout:** the steel grade (Spec) is optional; bars without it are stored without a grade.
  • **Grasshopper, AddEvidence:** an invalid identity id or evidence text is an error, no longer a warning.
  • **Grasshopper, CSC_Update:** after it replaces the source of a component, the remark and the end of the run ask you to save the definition, close it and open it again before clicking Apply: until then Rhino 8 opens the script editor of that component read-only and the component reports "Object reference not set to an instance of an object".
  • Grasshopper library: csc_gh 261102; CSC_Update brings it.
  • Component map: the layout now starts from a PCA initialisation instead of the spectral one, which failed on groups of near-identical elements and fell back to a random start. All positions on the map shift once with the first nightly run after the release.
  • Development: the development requirements are pinned exactly (pytest 9.1.1, pytest-xdist 3.8.0, coverage 7.16.2, flake8 7.4.1, invoke 3.0.3, requests 2.34.2, pyld 3.3.0, rdflib 7.6.0), and CI installs the same pytest. A cancelled sign-in in the Grasshopper tests no longer leaves an exception in a thread.

Server notes

  • In the server's frontend .env, take the version number out of BETA_BANNER_TEXT and BETA_LOGIN_MESSAGE, or write {version} in its place (for example BETA_BANNER_TEXT="VERSION {version}"). Restart the frontend.

Full history: CHANGELOG.md
